s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of skin lesions with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory results
salient_findings: Numerous irregular, erythematous papules and nodules on the abdomen and lower back
Leukopenia, anemia, mild thrombocytopenia, and neutropenia
Elevated C-reactive protein and alkaline phosphatase
key_facts: Skin lesions on abdomen and lower back
Denies weight loss, chills, abdominal pain, bleeding, or healing problems
Numerous moderately severe, irregular, erythematous papules and nodules on examination
Negative panel for sexually transmitted infections
Shave biopsy showed dense infiltrate of monotonous neoplastic cells

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory results, consistent with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Leukemia cutis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia, suggesting leukemia cutis

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with erythematous papules and nodules, consistent with mycosis fungoides

shortlist.label: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with dense infiltrate of monotonous neoplastic cells, consistent with blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm

shortlist.label: Acute myeloid leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal laboratory results, including leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia, suggesting acute myeloid leukemia

raw.rationale: The presence of a dense infiltrate of monotonous neoplastic cells with dispersed chromatin and a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio in the dermis, along with systemic symptoms such as leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia, is consistent with blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm, a rare and aggressive hematologic malignancy that often presents with skin involvement.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While cutaneous T-cell lymphoma can present with skin lesions, the biopsy findings and systemic symptoms in this case are more suggestive of a hematologic malignancy with specific dendritic cell involvement.

rejected.label: Leukemia cutis
rejected.why: Leukemia cutis refers to the infiltration of the skin by leukemic cells, but the specific findings in this case, including the type of cells seen on biopsy, point towards a more specific diagnosis of blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm.

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: Mycosis fungoides is the most common form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and typically has a more indolent course, with different biopsy findings that do not match the description provided.

rejected.label: Acute myeloid leukemia
rejected.why: While acute myeloid leukemia can cause skin lesions (leukemia cutis), the specific biopsy findings of monotonous neoplastic cells with dispersed chromatin and a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio are more characteristic of blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm.
